transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-27
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Lena Martinez (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Cho (Redwood SE), Asha Rao (Cerebrum Senior Cloud Eng), Tomás Rivera (NetOps Lead), Priya Nair (Director ML Platform), Ben Curtis (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick sync after last night's micro-kernel push where we saw intermittent token latency spikes and occasional egress reroutes. Focus: confirm immediate rollback, align on bench plan, and close telemetry gaps.

[00:00] Lena Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have a full room. quick agenda: rollbacks, telemetry, bench, security follow-ups.
[00:22] Asha Rao: yep thanks Lena, morning for us, we'll probably go through NetOps stuff first, we've got three incidents overnight, two were egress flaps and one was a latency burn.
[00:35] Jordan Patel: okay can you describe the egress flaps? were routes being withdrawn or is it BGP-ish?
[00:44] Tomás Rivera: it's not BGP, it's our cloud route priorities flipping, looks like the session with the Redwood Private edge re-established on a different path, so packets took a higher-latency hop, had some SYN retries. maybe related to the kernel changes you pushed.
[01:05] Evan Cho: we did a tiny micro-kernel tweak to the attention kernel selection logic last night, intended to reduce the L2 memcpy overhead under bursty loads. we pushed to canary then rolled to the pilot. seems like for your traffic shape it triggered an unexpected CPU steal pattern on the host side, which may have delayed the handshake for the VPC tunnel.
[01:36] Priya Nair: when you say CPU steal, is that inside our VPC or on Redwood nodes? I want to be clear for our infra team.
[01:45] Jordan Patel: sorry, that was on Redwood private nodes — the change changes how we pick kernels per sequence length so some hosts had slightly different jitter. It shouldn't change routing but the handshake window with your PSK-based tunnel may have been sensitive.
[02:04] Ben Curtis: just flagging security — we couldn't find certain span IDs in the telemetry to correlate auth retries. that made troubleshooting slower.
[02:15] Lena Martinez: understood. so immediate proposal: revert the micro-kernel change for the pilot for 24-48 hours, that's low-risk. run a KV-cache warmup test and a throughput bench to reproduce the spike, and expand telemetry to include span IDs and tunnel handshake events.
[02:36] Tomás Rivera: sounds reasonable. what does revert look like operationally for us? any downtime?
[02:44] Jordan Patel: no service window required, it's a version flip on the node pool and will roll in small batches — but we will coordinate a targeted window to keep you in the loop. expected impact: sub-second rolling transitions, we keep one pool in older version until canaries pass.
[03:05] Asha Rao: perfect — just give us the exact windows and we will open the firewall windows for the canaries.
[03:12] Lena Martinez: action: Lena will send rollback plan by EOD tomorrow. noted.
[03:20] [00:03:30] Priya Nair: on KV-cache warmup — we saw token latencies spike on cold prefixes. is there a recommended warmup script?
[03:31] Evan Cho: yes we have a warmup script that issues a mix of token prefixes across the model families to populate the KV cache; Jordan will supply a runbook. for your throughput bench we want a controlled 2-hour run with variable sequence lengths: 64/256/1024.
[03:52] Jordan Patel: i'll package the script and the docker runner, we can provide the expected CPU/memory sigs and a small parser for token latency.
[04:06] Tomás Rivera: can we run that from inside our VPC against the Redwood Private endpoint or do you prefer we use an external harness?
[04:14] Jordan Patel: either works — if inside VPC we get more realistic networking behavior. we'll send the runner as both an image and a small k8s job manifest.
[04:26] [00:05:00] Asha Rao: on telemetry gaps, Ben pointed out missing span IDs. we also couldn't map some requests back to your cost logs so we couldn't reconcile spikes to customer tokens.
[04:39] Ben Curtis: yeah the trace correlation ID was missing for about 17% of samples in last 6 hours. maybe the tracer wasn't propagated through the reroute.
[04:48] Evan Cho: noting that our tracer injects a header X-Rdw-Trace but some of your egress NAT translates headers — possible that header is dropped. we'll add ID into the body for redundancy and add span logs for tunnel handshake events.
[05:06] Priya Nair: if you add it to body we'll need to certify that there is no PII in there. keep it a UUID.
[05:13] Jordan Patel: agreed, just a correlation UUID, no payload.
[05:18] [00:06:00] Lena Martinez: security docs — Ben, what else do you need from us?
[05:25] Ben Curtis: SOC2 attestation yes, also KMS integration doc: we need to validate that keys never leave our KMS and how handshake secrets are derived. you mentioned HSM support last week?
[05:35] Evan Cho: we support customer-managed KMS via our Private control plane, we can push an HSM-backed key reference. will send a note on key derivation and that we don't get plaintext keys.
[05:44] Asha Rao: is there an audit log for key usage that we can ingest?
[05:49] Evan Cho: yes, we stream usage events to the project audit log; we'll include examples and a retention policy.
[05:56] [00:07:00] Tomás Rivera: back to routing flaps — do you have any logic that prefers cheaper egress by default? sometimes we've seen traffic get re-routed to a cheaper hop which added 80ms.
[06:09] Jordan Patel: routing policy is tiered: prefer local region low-latency path; fallback to burst cheaper capacity only under heavy load. however the micro-kernel change affected timing and caused some session resets which let fallback policy kick in.
[06:28] Priya Nair: so it's a timing sensitivity issue, not policy change.
[06:31] Jordan Patel: correct. we should see it fixed by reverting.
[06:36] [00:08:00] Asha Rao: what about throughput numbers — we need to know if dedicated reserved capacity would help us vs relying on shared pilot. do you have a quick showback for the current pilot?
[06:47] Lena Martinez: we can produce a showback: tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency by model config. i'll include a cost trade-off for reserved pool (Redwood Dedicated) vs hosted pilot.
[06:58] Priya Nair: timeline question: if we do a short pilot extension, what's the path to Dedicated?
[07:06] Lena Martinez: typical path: pilot -> 4-week bake -> commitment conversation. given your scale and compliance needs, we can run parallel testing of Dedicated capacity in a private VPC to show deterministic latency.
[07:20] Ben Curtis: one more security ask: proof of attestation for our auditors that keys are not exported. a short letter or whitepaper will do.
[07:28] Evan Cho: yep we'll include a KMS/HSM whitepaper and our SOC2 scope doc.
[07:32] [00:09:00] Jordan Patel: returning to bench specifics: for the throughput run we want to capture per-token CPU, NVMe IO, and network RTTs. do you have a metrics exporter already?
[07:45] Asha Rao: we use Prometheus internally and have a Grafana stack. can you ship a Prom exporter or do you push metrics to our project?
[07:55] Jordan Patel: we can publish Prom scrape endpoints inside the VPC or ship a sidecar exporter. shipping a Prom endpoint is simplest for you.
[08:03] Tomás Rivera: we'll prefer scrape endpoints. note we'll need mutual TLS to scrape — can't have open endpoints.
[08:10] Evan Cho: we can generate a client cert for your scrape, or we can run an exporter that authenticates via the same PSK tunnel.
[08:16] [00:10:00] Priya Nair: are there any config knobs we should change to reduce jitter during the bench? e.g., prefetch warmup, batch size caps?
[08:27] Jordan Patel: yes set max_batch=64 for the bench and enable prefetched KV cache warmup, also set response streaming buffer to 256KB. we'll give you recommended values per model family.
[08:38] Asha Rao: will changing batch size impact cost a lot?
[08:41] Lena Martinez: batch size affects unit cost but for benching we recommend pushing higher batch for throughput tests; we'll run a cost-normalised comparison after.
[08:53] [00:11:00] Tomás Rivera: any chance the CDN in front of your Private endpoint added variance? we saw cache misses that were unexpected.
[09:01] Jordan Patel: the Private endpoints sometimes sit behind an edge proxy for routing choice; we'll check cache TTLs and exclude CDN from the bench.
[09:10] Evan Cho: note: the CDN is only for static assets; dynamic calls hit the inference nodes directly, but we will validate edge proxies.
[09:20] [00:12:00] Lena Martinez: okay rounding up the immediate next steps: rollback micro-kernel, send rollback plan, Jordan sends warmup script and runner, Red send telemetry mapping and security pack. schedule bench (2 hours) week of 9/6.
[09:36] Priya Nair: need to lock the bench date asap, i'll block tentative windows on calendar after Lena shares availability.
[09:44] Ben Curtis: one security caveat: we need to validate any change doesn't alter encryption-at-rest or key usage.
[09:52] Evan Cho: acknowledged, no key material will move during rollback. it's a binary flip of runtime selection.
[10:00] [00:13:00] Asha Rao: if you revert, will you also pause any auto-scaling policies that could spin new nodes with the new kernel?
[10:09] Jordan Patel: yes we will pin the node image for the pilot pool and pause autoscaler for the 24-48 window.
[10:16] Tomás Rivera: great. we'll also pin our VPC route table during the test to avoid reflexive changes from our side.
[10:23] [00:14:00] Lena Martinez: any other blockers?
[10:28] Priya Nair: none from our side. just need the security pack and VPC route ask.
[10:33] Jordan Patel: i'll follow up with the exporter manifest for Prom and a k8s job for the warmup.
[10:39] [00:15:00] Lena Martinez: thanks everyone. quick recap and owners before close.
[10:44] -- Recap --
[10:45] Lena Martinez: Lena: send rollback plan by 2026-08-28. Jordan: warmup script + runner by 2026-08-30 and exporter manifest. Asha: share route table screenshots by 2026-08-31. Ben: confirm KMS constraints by 2026-09-02. Plan bench week of 2026-09-06.
[11:08] Tomás Rivera: ack.
[11:10] Priya Nair: ack.
[11:12] Ben Curtis: ack, will look for SOC2 + KMS docs.
[11:15] Lena Martinez: I'll also attach a short showback doc with cost/latency tradeoffs for Dedicated vs Pilot.
[11:24] [00:19:00] Jordan Patel: final note — we'll run a focused 30-min smoke test after rollback to confirm handshake stability before the 2-hour bench.
[11:35] Evan Cho: noted.
[11:40] [00:20:00] Meeting ended: 16:53 UTC

References/links mentioned:
